title: Why he quit Ellington
summary: He was sick of hypocrisy, exploitation and deceit, and Bigard's wish for him to play is relayed.

blocks.x: Barnaby Guard asked me to tell you that he sure wishes you'd play your horn.

Oh, yes. We'd get a little group and go to Europe, and in the words of the modernists, we could have a ball. But, no. I'm -- when you get to a certain period in life I think you should sort of sit down and let the rest of the world carry on.
But you have not -- your plan wasn't to retire in 1970, was it? Your plan was to merely quit Duke Ellington?
I was -- yes, I was just sick and tired of all of that hypocrisy, exploitation, deceit, and things -- everything that was going on. And so I just --
You're talking about within the band?

Yes, with the whole game. It's -- very little of it is honest, and it's nothing but exploiting a few people for the benefit of a few. And I just can't see it, and can't agree with it. So, step aside and let the circus go on.
